title: dnaa-11 — RIDA+SeqA tighten control but RIDA drains the DnaA-ATP fraction (recalibration needed)
caption: 3-way progression (seeds 0/1/2). LEFT: max oriC — async alone over-replicates (dnaa-9, red), SeqA controls it (dnaa-10, green, max 3), RIDA+SeqA is tightest (dnaa-11, blue, max 2). RIGHT: total DnaA-ATP fraction — in band with SeqA (hydrolysis 0.025), but adding RIDA DRAINS it out of band (~0.01); recalibrating the hydrolysis rate down (k_h~0.015) restores it to ~0.37.
interpretation: RIDA and SeqA together fully control the asynchronous over-replication, but RIDA perturbs a prior criterion (the DnaA-ATP fraction) — a live example of the controlled-progression recalibration step. RIDA also suppresses the asynchrony (keeps DnaA-ATP low), so SeqA alone (dnaa-10) remains the minimal control that both fixes over-replication and preserves the async.
